context:
Goal: finished lane sessions get archived with no one keeping a list by hand (your 11:31 CST ask).
Problem (goal): 32 idle lanes piled up in the coordinator's handoff, because the archive list is kept by hand. The decision also asks a test nobody can apply ("topic has no queued step"): no step file records a topic.
Based on (measured): two planners, Nov 6. Archiving one lane is two tool calls. The cases that need judgment (unpushed work, records on another branch, a lane waiting on you) can be detected and skipped, not reasoned through.
Departs from: decision session-tiers lines 63-66, the coordinator's hand list and the topic test — the list is worked out from live sessions and landed steps.

In a and b the topic test goes. Meanwhile: lane idle-lane-archive builds the list command, which all three options use.
lastAnswer: a (owner chat 11:38 CST Nov 6, relayed by the coordinator): "A is fine the batch runner keeps archiving more automatically". Lane idle-lane-archive rewrites decision session-tiers; open until its PR merges.

options.gain: No extra session. After each merge the merge tool works out the list, so it is never stale or forgotten; judgment cases are skipped and named.
options.label: The batch runner archives, from a worked-out list
options.lose: The batch runner does a little more after each merge.

options.gain: Merges and archiving never compete for one session's attention.
options.label: A standing janitor session
options.lose: One more standing session to pay for, for about two turns of work per batch. It needs a wake; a timer is barred (rule outcomes-mechanize-rules), so it wakes on each merge anyway.

options.gain: The session that started a lane ends it.
options.label: The coordinator archives its own lanes
options.lose: Two calls per lane in the session that talks with you, against your Nov 1 ruling to keep it focused.

ref: owner ask 11:31 CST Nov 6; step idle-lane-archive
title: Who archives finished lane sessions: the batch runner, a janitor session, or the coordinator?
why: Recommended: a. Your janitor idea, but run by the session that already wakes on each merge, so it costs no new session.
